name: HiP-CT organ: brain (fixed)
description: A formalin-fixed brain, as HiP-CT's are: grey matter tan, white matter cream; colours measured on fixed brain slices.

reference.title: File:Human brain frontal (coronal) section.JPG
reference.author: John A. Beal, PhD, Dept. of Cellular Biology & Anatomy, LSU Health Sciences Center Shreveport
reference.shows: One whole coronal slice through thalamus and brainstem: cortex, white matter, thalamus, lateral ventricles.
reference.notes: Normal adult brain; formalin-fixed appearance (not stated on the file page). Grey/white contrast is low at this resolution (original is only 702 px wide, kept at native size). Red inset at lower left is a locator drawing: avoid.

reference.title: File:Human Brain.jpg
reference.author: Suseno
reference.shows: Whole fresh autopsy brain, superior/lateral convexity with leptomeninges and engorged surface vessels; gloved hand holding it.
reference.notes: Fresh autopsy brain (no disease stated). 'grey matter (cortex)' boxes here are the pial surface of gyri seen through the thin leptomeninges, between surface vessels, so they include a little capillary red. The pale bulging area at lower left is not interpreted (possibly stripped/oedematous tissue) and is not boxed. Steel table is not used as neutral because of its scratches and blood smears.

reference.title: File:Brain autopsy lateral view.jpg
reference.author: Jensflorian
reference.shows: Lateral view of a whole formalin-fixed brain with intact arachnoid over the gyri.
reference.notes: Formalin-fixed (per file description). Cortex boxes are on gyral crowns through the arachnoid, avoiding glare streaks; the 'meninges' box is on the bluish translucent arachnoid bridging a sulcus. Same author has top and bottom views of the same brain (not used).

reference.title: File:Coronal cross-section of human brain.jpg
reference.author: Rajalakshmi L. Nair et al.
reference.shows: Single formalin-fixed slice through the frontal lobes/basal ganglia region: cortex, white matter, corpus callosum, deep grey nuclei.
reference.notes: From a case report (Nair et al., CC BY 2.0); caption says normal grey and white matter but diffuse cortical oedema with small ventricles, so cortex may be a little paler/swollen than normal. Deep grey boxes are on the large tan nuclei below the corpus callosum (thalamus/basal ganglia; level is not certain).

reference.title: File:Autopsy brain.jpg
reference.author: Neuropathologyblog
reference.shows: Two formalin-fixed autopsy brains, inferior (basal) view.
reference.notes: NOT normal: left brain is from an 82-year-old with spinocerebellar ataxia type 6 (cerebellar atrophy), right is a 96-year-old with Alzheimer disease. Boxes are only on the cerebral cortex surface of the left brain (cerebrum not expected to be grossly abnormal in SCA6). Blue background may bias white balance.

name: HiP-CT organ: heart
description: A heart: myocardium red-brown, epicardial fat yellow, valves and fibrous tissue pale.

reference.title: File:Gross pathology of papillary muscle infarction, overview.jpg
reference.author: Mikael Häggström, M.D.
reference.shows: Short-axis slice of the left ventricle with epicardial fat at the lower left.
reference.notes: Autopsy heart with a fresh infarct of one papillary muscle (dark area, upper centre of the cavity); boxes are on the free LV wall away from it. Appears unfixed (not stated).

reference.title: File:Gross pathology of old myocardial infarction, original.jpg
reference.author: Mikael Häggström, M.D.
reference.shows: Short-axis slice through both ventricles (RV at right) with epicardial fat at the rim.
reference.notes: Old (scarred) infarct in the posterior LV wall (pale areas at the lower edge); boxes avoid it. Appears unfixed (not stated).

reference.title: File:Lammherz.jpg
reference.author: Rainer Zenz
reference.shows: Lamb heart halved lengthwise: cut ventricular myocardium, trabeculated endocardium, white fat at the base.
reference.notes: ANIMAL (lamb), used for cut myocardium under neutral studio light. Lamb fat is white, unlike yellow human epicardial fat; the fat box is kept but should not stand for human fat colour.

reference.title: File:Pig heart.JPG
reference.author: Gaisjonke
reference.shows: Partially cut pig heart, outer epicardial surface of the ventricles (dark red-purple) with a little basal fat.
reference.notes: ANIMAL (pig); fills the gap for unfixed outer myocardial surface under neutral light. Glare streaks on the left ventricle are avoided.

reference.title: File:Heart dissection.jpg
reference.author: Anatomist90
reference.shows: Embalmed cadaver heart in situ with opened pericardium: yellow epicardial fat, grey myocardium, great vessels.
reference.notes: Embalmed (fixed) dissection-room specimen. The 'valves and fibrous tissue' box is on the opened fibrous pericardium, not a valve. Boxes avoid labels and arrows. Native 960 px.

reference.shows: Freshly resected human left lower lobe (with tumour) on a green drape after VATS; pleural surface.
reference.notes: Fresh surgical specimen; the lobe contains a tumour and is collapsed and congested, so it is darker red than inflated normal lung. Boxes are on the smooth pleural surface away from the tumour area and black anthracotic spots.

reference.title: File:Pig lungs (1).jpg

reference.shows: Several fresh pig lungs (pleural surface) and a trachea in a white tray.

reference.title: File:An open-cutted lung.jpg

reference.shows: Fresh pig lung lobe cut open along a bronchus: cut parenchyma above and below an opened bronchus.

name: HiP-CT organ: kidney
description: A kidney: red-brown cortex and medulla, yellow sinus fat, pale capsule and vessel walls.

reference.title: File:Renal oncocytoma.jpg
reference.author: Emmanuelm (English Wikipedia)
reference.shows: Bisected nephrectomy specimen: renal oncocytoma (brown, left) beside normal kidney with cortex, pyramids and sinus fat.
reference.notes: Boxes only on the normal kidney (upper right and lower right) away from the tumour. Cortex is a thin band at the convexity; medulla boxes are on the striated pyramids. Neutral box on the white ruler strip between ticks. Native 600 px (500 px rendition used).

reference.title: A GRIA2 and PAX8-positive renal solitary fibrous tumor with NAB2-STAT6 gene fusion (Diagn Pathol 2015;10:155), figure 13000_2015_386_Fig2_HTML.jpg
reference.author: Authors of Diagn Pathol 2015;10:155 (PMC4559176)
reference.shows: Cut section of a resected kidney with a whitish solitary fibrous tumour (lower right) and normal dark red parenchyma, pelvis and sinus fat.
reference.notes: Only 358 px wide. Tumour (white, lower right) not boxed. Cortex/medulla boundary is indistinct at this resolution, so only cortex boxes near the capsule. Neutral box on the white ruler. Licence: PMC open-access record gives 'CC BY' (version taken as 4.0; check the article).

reference.title: Back-Table Repair of Parenchymal and Collecting System Injury of a Living Donor Kidney (Cureus 2026;18(8):e113899), figure cureus-0018-00000113899-i05.webp
reference.author: Authors of Cureus 2026;18(8):e113899 (PMC13537905)
reference.shows: Living-donor kidney in the recipient after reperfusion: red outer capsular surface with the repaired area (dark, arrows).
reference.notes: Living, perfused kidney: capsule colour is in-vivo. Boxes avoid the repair site, blue arrows, glare and blood. Neutral box on white gauze (may carry a faint pink tinge). Used because surgical-light images were the only fresh human capsule views found. Licence: PMC open-access record gives 'CC BY' (version taken as 4.0; check the article).

reference.title: File:Gross pathology of nephrosclerosis.jpg
reference.author: Mikael Häggström, M.D.
reference.shows: Outer capsular surface of an autopsy kidney (capsule stripped) with a ruler.
reference.notes: NOT normal: nephrosclerosis gives a finely granular surface, but the colour is representative of decapsulated cortex surface. Only 500 px rendition. Neutral on the white background.

reference.title: File:Kidney of lamb 11.jpg
reference.author: Jurfeld
reference.shows: Lamb kidney halved (left) and whole (right): dark cortex, pale-pink medulla/crest, white sinus fat; capsule surface on the whole kidney.
reference.notes: ANIMAL (sheep): unipapillary kidney with a single renal crest, so medulla layout differs from human, but tissue colours are useful.

reference.title: File:Pig-kidney.JPG
reference.author: Thor-Rune Hansen (ThorRune)
reference.shows: Fresh pig kidney sliced open lengthwise: red-brown cortex, darker red medullary pyramids, pale sinus fat.
reference.notes: ANIMAL (pig), multipapillary like human. Neutral on paper towel at lower left (towel is slightly warm/yellow).
